identification.title: All Sufficient Merit
identification.notes: Written by Shane Barnard, Bethany Barnard and Bryan Fowler; copyright 2023 Songs From Wellhouse and More Songs From Wellhouse (Capitol CMG Publishing), Be Essential Songs and bryanfowlersongs (Essential Music Publishing); CCLI 7212933. The list's guess of Shane & Shane / Bryan Fowler is right but incomplete: Bethany Barnard is a co-writer. It is a new song, one of two newly written tracks on the live album recorded at Liberty University and released as a single on 3 February 2023. No source read says it is built on an older hymn; the title echoes hymn vocabulary but no hymn source was found. Reviewed as the song, not any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: Three stanzas, a two-line chorus repeated after stanzas 2 and 3 and again at the end, and a short closing tag repeating the last idea. Stanza 1 sets the believer's own righteousness aside for Christ's; stanza 2 names the incarnation, sinless life and atoning death; stanza 3 has the believer clothed in Christ's righteousness and standing accepted before God. The resurrection and Christ's return are not named.

claims.claim: Righteousness is an inheritance, not earned; the believer forfeits his own at the cross, where Christ's merit did what he could not.
claims.subject: Justification by grace alone

claims.claim: The Maker entered time, lived without sin and died as the spotless Lamb, since the law could not save.
claims.subject: Incarnation, sinless life and atoning death

claims.claim: Christ's work is finished, the debt is paid and his merit is counted as the believer's.
claims.subject: Finished work and imputed righteousness

claims.claim: The believer lays aside his own works and boasting, is clothed in Christ's righteousness and has no fear of judgment.
claims.subject: Imputation and assurance

claims.claim: In life and death the believer is confident, and will stand accepted before God's throne, thanking Jesus for the cross.
claims.subject: Final acceptance and gratitude

strengths.title: Standing rests wholly on Christ's merit
strengths.explanation: The song sets the believer's own righteousness and works aside and puts his acceptance on Christ's merit alone, counted as his. That is justification by grace through faith, stated as a ground rather than a feeling.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Righteousness apart from the law, received through faith in Christ.

strengths.title: Incarnation, sinless life and atoning death
strengths.explanation: Stanza 2 names the Maker entering time, living without sin and dying as the spotless Lamb. Calling the Creator the one who died is orthodox incarnation language.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The sinless one made sin for us so that we become the righteousness of God.

strengths.title: Imputed righteousness removes fear of judgment
strengths.explanation: The believer is clothed in Christ's righteousness and expects to stand accepted before God, with the cross as the cause of his thanks.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Clothed with garments of salvation and the robe of righteousness.

doctrinesAffirmed: Justification by grace alone through faith
Atoning death of the spotless Lamb
Assurance and final acceptance before God
theological.assessment: Nothing false or misleading was found in the words. The song locates the believer's standing in Christ's merit and finished work, sets aside his own works, and names the incarnation, sinless life and atoning death. The resurrection and return are not named, which is an absence rather than an error.

strengths.title: Fits a service of the cross and communion
strengths.explanation: Its content on Christ's sacrifice and the believer's acceptance suits Good Friday, communion and any time the gospel is restated for the room.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published original key is E (also F) in 6/8 per PraiseCharts; the live recording sits in lower keys. No chart was read; test the key with the room.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: A two-line chorus returns after stanzas 2 and 3 and at the end, with a short tag, so the central claim of the finished work is repeated deliberately.
communal.assessment: Moderate-length lines and a repeated chorus make it strong for group singing, though it is long overall and sits slightly high for some voices. Judged from the words and structure; no chart was read.

strengths.title: Christ's work is plainly stated
strengths.explanation: The stanzas name Christ's incarnation, sinless life and death and say what his merit does for the believer, so the grounds of salvation are not left to inference.

clarity.assessment: Clear in its claim. The title and some vocabulary, such as merit and imputed righteousness, are older churchly terms that may need a word of explanation.

synthesis.summary: A 2023 song by Shane and Bethany Barnard and Bryan Fowler setting Christ's merit against the believer's own works as the ground of acceptance. It names the incarnation, sinless life and atoning death and speaks of imputed righteousness and final acceptance before God. Nothing false or misleading was found; the resurrection and return go unnamed.

scriptureReferences.relevance: Salvation by grace, not works - the contrast the song draws.
One sacrifice that perfects for all time - the finished work.
Peace and standing with God through Christ.
